2610.11374.title: Rethinking Contrastive Loss in CLIP Post-training: A Complementary Framework with Frozen Text Encoder
2610.11374.paper_summary: CLIP serves as a foundational vision-language model and the de facto vision encoder for downstream VLMs such as LLaVA. Post-training offers a lightweight route to refine CLIP, but recent work argues that the standard contrastive loss is unsuitable for post-training due to catastrophic forgetting under small batches, motivating designs that abandon the contrastive objective in favor of distillation. We revisit this premise and find that, for the InfoNCE objective, the reported forgetting is driven primarily not by insufficient negatives but by an inappropriate magnitude of the contrastive temperature $τ$: with $τ$ set sufficiently small, contrastive post-training improves rather than degrades the pretrained CLIP, which we explain through the temperature dependence of the InfoNCE gradient. Building on this finding, we propose \textbf{ComCLIP}, a lightweight single-epoch post-training recipe that freezes CLIP's text encoder---so the refined vision encoder is a drop-in replacement with unchanged architecture and inference cost---and trains the vision encoder with a properly-tempered contrastive loss, an MSE anchoring loss against the original CLIP, and a relational distillation loss from DINOv2. Over multiple seeds, ComCLIP matches the self-distillation baseline CLIP-Refine on zero-shot classification while significantly improving the transferability of visual features, measured by linear probing ($48.99$ vs.\ $42.28$ on ViT-B/16), and on ViT-L/14 it also improves MMVP over CLIP-Refine ($24.20$ vs.\ $19.01$); CLIP-Refine remains stronger on image-text retrieval. Used as a drop-in vision encoder for LLaVA-1.5-7B without re-aligning the projector or LLM, ComCLIP yields no net change across $8$ VLM benchmarks, i.e., the refinement does not break downstream compatibility. Code and models are available at https://github.com/showstarpro/ComCLIP.git.
2610.11374.paper_summary_zh: CLIP 作為一個基礎的視覺-語言模型以及下游 VLM（視覺語言模型）如 LLaVA 的事實上視覺編碼器。後訓練提供了一種輕量化的路徑來精煉 CLIP，但最近的研究認為標準的對比損失不適合後訓練，因為在小批量下會發生災難性遺忘，這促使設計放棄對比目標而轉向蒸餾。我們重新審視這一前提，發現對於 InfoNCE 目標，報告的遺忘主要不是由於負樣本不足，而是由於對比溫度 $τ$ 的不當大小：當 $τ$ 設置得足夠小時，對比後訓練會改善而不是惡化預訓練的 CLIP，我們通過 InfoNCE 梯度的溫度依賴性來解釋這一點。在此基礎上，我們提出了 \textbf{ComCLIP}，這是一種輕量級的單輪次後訓練配方，凍結 CLIP 的文本編碼器——因此精煉的視覺編碼器是一個架構和推理成本不變的替代品——並使用適當調整的對比損失、針對原始 CLIP 的均方誤差錨定損失以及來自 DINOv2 的關係蒸餾損失來訓練視覺編碼器。在多個隨機種子下，ComCLIP 在零-shot 分類上與自蒸餾基線 CLIP-Refine 相匹配，同時顯著改善了視覺特徵的可轉移性，通過線性探測測量（$48.99$ 對 $42.28$ 在 ViT-B/16 上），在 ViT-L/14 上，它也改善了 CLIP-Refine 的 MMVP（$24.20$ 對 $19.01$）；CLIP-Refine 在圖像-文本檢索上仍然更強。作為 LLaVA-1.5-7B 的即插即用視覺編碼器，未重新對齊投影器或 LLM，ComCLIP 在 $8$ 個 VLM 基準測試中沒有產生淨變化，即精煉不破壞下游兼容性。代碼和模型可在 https://github.com/showstarpro/ComCLIP.git 獲得。
